## Step 8g3-pre: a card figure's length step (2026-11-10; D-2026-11-10-16)
`data-figure-step` (`markFigureStep`, `FIGURE_STEP_CEILINGS` = 9, 11, 14, 17,
21 in `src/ui/render.ts`) splits the card ladder's tier 0 into three steps a
look may size by, and keeps tiers 1–3 as steps 4–6, on the face's figure,
"You pay", a pay sheet's figure and the selection strip's total. A look may
size a figure at any step, so every step is a rule no pass measures until a
fixture paints it.

### What the probe reads
- **Five geometry-only fixtures**, each at the widest figure its step holds:
  `item-listing-figure-11` (`999,999,999`, and "You pay" at the same step),
  `item-quote-figure-11` (`₩99,999,999`, the sign drawn by the machine's
  fallback at about 1em), `pay-several-figure-steps` (two won quotes, lines of
  11 and 14 characters, its XEC figure 18 characters at 0.03 won a XEC),
  `pay-several-strip-11` (`₩99,999,999`) and `pay-several-strip-17`
  (`元9,999,999,999.99`). On `STATE_SCREENS`, `GEOMETRY_ONLY_SCREENS` and the
  narrow pass (45 → 50 screens). With the ladder's own fixtures they paint
  every step on all four places on every look (`every-figure-step-is-painted-on-every-surface`
  in happy-dom; in Chrome, the pass line below).
- **`a-card-figure-stands-inside-its-row` reads the strip total**, strictly,
  against its own `.sel-totalblk` (`strip`). No card rule read it before.
  Run alone on main's tree first (2026-11-10, the whole runner, that one line
  added to `CARD_FIGURES`): every pass green on every look, 54 strip reads on
  the phone pass and on the narrow pass, the contrast dump unchanged. It also
  counts the four places per step (`cardFigureStepByClass`) and fails a row
  that holds a figure and carries no step.
- **The step half of `a-card-figure-steps-down-on-every-look`**
  (`cardStepLadderFaults`): per look, per variant, for the four ladder figures
  and the strip total, no step paints larger than the smallest size the step
  before it painted. No "the last is smaller" half. **On the phone passes
  only** (390 and 360), as the tier half: a desk rule keyed on a step is held
  by the rules that read a figure where it stands, and by no ladder compare.
- **Owed** (`FIGURE_STEPS_OWED`, `CARD_STEP_LADDERS_OWED`): the phone and
  narrow passes owe `face`, `paid`, `pay` and `strip` at steps 1–6 on every
  look they painted, and the five step ladders compared over `123456`.

### The clean tree
Pass line at 390: figure steps read face:1 66, face:2–6 18 each, paid:1 57,
paid:2–6 9 each, pay:1 60, pay:2 18, pay:3 9, pay:4 18, pay:5 9, pay:6 27,
strip:1 18, strip:2–4 9 each, strip:5 18, strip:6 9 · step ladders compared:
25 (five looks, five figures). At 360 the same but face:1 42 and paid:1 33.
No failure. The contrast dump is the main tree's box for box (15,018 boxes
over 823 jobs, `contrast-dump.mjs`: 0 moved, 0 added, 0 removed). The whole
run 227.7s of 300 at three tabs, load 5.61 at the start and 5.80 at the end
(main's tree with the strip read, the same hour: 234.5s, load 1.27 → 7.82;
one run each, not an A/B pair). The narrow pass 28.3s on its tab (25.7s for 45
screens on main's tree).

### The belt
A first-party rule naming the step names it on the subject's compound or an
ancestor of it, joined by descendant or child combinators alone, never inside
a functional pseudo-class, never over a pseudo-element, and sets `font-size`
and `line-height` alone (`figureStepProblems` in `scripts/workshop-css.mjs`,
`a-figure-step-only-sizes-a-figure`). Red: the critic's three plants (the
final-payment line hidden under `:has(.pay-x[data-figure-step='4'])`, a
face's Buy at step 3, the whole stall restyled at step 6), `:not()`, `:is()`
and `:where()`, a sibling by `+` and by `~`, a pseudo-element, a `display`, a
colour beside a size, a `font` shorthand, a custom property, the name in
capitals and escaped, and the `:has()` plant inside a media block. Taken:
`.t-x .face-x[data-figure-step='3'] { font-size: 30px }` and five more sizes.
The kit refuses the hook outright (`FIRST_PARTY_HOOK`, case-blind since the
critic's P2-2: `[DATA-FIGURE-STEP]` and the other hooks in capitals are
refused too).

What the belt does not say, stated (the 8g3 build critic's P2-1 and P3): a
step does not only size a figure. Its font size reaches every font-relative
length (`em`, `lh`) a rule writes under its row, so a look can grow or move a
box at one step only. The honest sentences on the pay sheets are read by the
contrast pass only at steps 1 and 6; steps 2-5 are painted only on
geometry-only screens (`pay-inr`, `pay-figure-14`, `pay-figure-17`,
`pay-long-figure`, `pay-several-figure-steps`), to be closed in 8g3 (PLAN §
Open). The belt accepts `font-size: 0` on non-money words under a step row (a
face's "from", a unit, the strip's note), as at rest on main. The census test
does not see an object-key write (`Object.assign(el.dataset, { figureStep })`).
The owed counts are summed over variants, so a worn-only rule at one step is
masked by the bare paint.

### Not read, stated
- A length no fixture paints within a step: each step is painted at its
  band's widest in the widest glyphs, so a look that sizes by step is held at
  each step's worst case, and within a step the tag does not vary. A fallback
  glyph another machine draws wider (`₩`, `元`) is the per-OS gap §6 already
  carries.
- The step ladder at desk widths (above), and the Pay several line, the Pay
  several total and the chosen line, which carry no step.
- The same `:has()` road through `data-price-tier` (from 15 characters) and
  the stream card's `data-tier`: older, open (PLAN § Open).

## The look run, and the probe's time by look (2026-11-11; D-2026-11-11-04)

The probe-prune plan's O1 and O2, with its critic's fixes; not its O3: the
tracked fixture stays in the default `pnpm test:layout`, which is unchanged.

### O1: where the time goes, by look
The runner timed passes and phases, never looks, so every per-look figure the
plan priced was a subtraction. It now prints, on every run:

- **`geometry by look`**: each geometry pass's measuring split by the look the
  page was measuring (`lookMs` and `measureMs` in the probe's verdict: the
  main loop's screens, the try-on's stress names, the record road and the
  billboard), page seconds, with what is no look's (the faces, the reads after
  the loop) as its own figure, and each pass's split under it. Clocks, left
  out of the geometry canary's comparison (`geometryRecordDiffers`).
- **`by look`** under the contrast phase table: every phase split by the look
  of the job it ran inside (an `AsyncLocalStorage` around each job; a phase
  outside any job, a page load or the plan reads, is `(shared)`), each look's
  total and its jobs' own tab time. Every phase now goes through one adder
  (`addPhase`), the eight that wrote `phases` by hand included, which writes
  the total and the look's part together, so they agree by construction (the
  first build printed an `(unattributed)` row that "must read 0", which could
  read nothing else; the critic's P3, dropped). Phases nest (`art off` holds
  captures), so a look's total can pass its jobs' time. Tab time is read under
  contention: the private look at 0x04's contrast jobs read 117.7s, 129.1s and
  133.7s on three runs, so a figure is a run's, not the look's marginal cost.
- **`carried looks:`** each carried look's geometry (page seconds) and
  contrast jobs (tab seconds) beside every look's.

Pure halves: `scripts/look-timing.mjs`, test `look-timing.test.mjs`. Proved
inert: the default run's contrast dump against main's, 15,018 boxes identical,
0 moved, added or removed (`node scripts/contrast-dump.mjs`).

Measured (this Mac, 6 cores, 8 GiB, three tabs), the default run with the
private look at 0x04 selected (251.1s; load 3.3 to 6.3): its geometry 20.7s of
296.8s page time, its contrast jobs 117.7s of 344.9s tab time (Neo 104.0s,
Rural 57.4s, Modern 43.4s, the skeleton 22.4s); the art-off frames (30.6s), its
look pseudos (19.0s) and 1c (8.2s) are its own. The default run without a
selection (225.0s; load 2.8 to 6.2): the tracked fixture's geometry 50.6s of
315.6s, its contrast jobs 60.4s of 253.5s.

### O2: `pnpm test:layout:look`
`node scripts/layout-check.mjs --looks carried`. Under a selection it measures
the private looks the selection carries; with none, the tracked fixture. Each
carried look is measured in full: every geometry pass, every screen, every
variant and every contrast and transparency job the ordinary run gives it,
held to every per-look owe it has there (`probeCoverageGaps`,
`look-tallies.mjs`: its own line-skip ceiling, clip ratio, codes owed by name,
wall controls, its sign's name, the try-on's stress names and, for a paid
look, the record road). Of the public looks (the shipped three and the
skeleton) it paints only the screens whose tree depends on what the build
carries (`CARRIED_SCREENS`, `layout/carriedScreens.ts`), on every pass that
measures them, bare and worn, and their contrast jobs there.

**Which screens: found, not read off `render.ts`.**
`a-public-screen-is-the-same-whatever-the-build-carries`
(`layout/carriedScreensCheck.ts`, four files of a quarter of the screens each):
every probe screen on every public look that can wear it, bare, each row alone
and every all-worn state (`layout/variants.ts`, a superset of what any pass
paints), painted in happy-dom in a build carrying no private look and again
with the private-looks module mocked to the tracked fixture; the trees (the
document head and the painted root, as a digest) must be identical except on
the listed screens, and every listed screen must differ (a stale entry is
red), for each build compared. With a selection named, the comparison is
made a second time over the selected private looks, read as the build and the
guards read them (`privateLookReads`), so a slice that gives the private look
at 0x04 a row, a mood or a token is held to the list on the run that carries
it (the probe-split critic's P2-2; with no selection, the fixture's alone).
The list today is one screen, `publish-name`: the name sheet's picker
holds one button per carried look, and a carrying build adds its
`look-status` line. The door differs too, but only on a look the door never
wears (`canWear`), so it is not painted. Red: a planted `LOOK_ROWS.length` on
the sign's box fails 700 paints of one quarter; `activity` planted on the list
fails it as stale; a selected build whose mock did not take (a module
carrying nothing) fails as stale for that build. Cost, measured in `beforeAll`:
27–29s a file on four workers with the fixture alone (62s on one worker), and
45–48s with the private look at 0x04 selected; the timeout is 240s.

**The plan splits by look.** `the-contrast-plan-splits-by-look`
(`layout/contrastPlanSplit.private.test.ts`): over the looks a build carrying
the fixture measures, the ordinary plan's job keys are exactly the public
looks' plan's and each carried look's, no key in two, for every way the
sheet-naming inputs (`namesCopied`, `namesStep`) can fall; and the look run's
plan (`carriedContrastPlan`) is the ordinary plan's own jobs of the carried
looks and of every look on a listed screen, in its order. Red: a planted
`looks.length > 1` on one screen fails 16 of its 18 cases.

**The look run's boxes are the ordinary run's.** `node
scripts/contrast-dump.mjs --within <look run> <ordinary run>` (kinds
`carried+<classes>` and `shipped+<the same classes>`): every job of the look
run is a job of the ordinary run with the same record, and every box of those
jobs the same box with the same worst, both ways (`compareWithin`, test
`a-look-run-is-the-ordinary-run-on-its-own-jobs`); and every job the ordinary
run gave a carried look, or any look on a listed screen, is a job of the look
run (`jobsDropped`, the critic's P3: the first build checked one way). Measured: the private look
at 0x04, 119 jobs (its 105, the public looks' 14 on `publish-name`), 2,017
boxes identical; the fixture, 182 jobs (168 and 14), 3,194 boxes identical.
The geometry's per-look tallies for a carried look read the same in both runs
(3a's elements per pass, the line skips, 1a's points behind a clip). One job
record differed on the first try and was fixed: the look run read Grid
horizon's worst on Neo's worn `publish-name` jobs, where the ordinary run reads
it on the owner's three jobs alone (`readsHorizonWorst` now reads a public
look's job as the shipped run does).

**What changed in the guard, by name.**
- The page (`?looks=carried`, `measureCarriedOnly` in `layout/looks.ts`):
  `measuredLooks()` is the carried looks, `looksFor(screen)` every look on a
  listed screen, `paintedLooks()` every look the page paints; the verdict
  echoes the list (`carriedOnly`), and the runner refuses a pass whose echo is
  not the mode it asked for or not the list another page read
  (`carriedEchoWrong`). What a pass adds to the cross-look owes (the
  decorations worn, the outlined targets owed a ring read) is a fully measured
  look's (`measuredInFull`): on the first try Neo worn on `publish-name` owed
  the rain and the horizon on no job, and six outlined lines nobody read.
- Expected classes per pass: the public classes only on a pass that measured
  a listed screen (`sheetClassesWrong(painted, witnessed)`); the transparency
  pass the carried looks alone.
- `probeCoverageGaps`' `witnessClasses`: the public looks painted on the
  listed screens owe no per-look read (the 14 loops over `report.sheetClasses`
  read `owing`), and the public looks' sum of the wall's controls is skipped;
  `shippedClasses` is empty and `skeleton` false, so the door's minis, the
  shipped rows' sizes and the skeleton's ladder are the ordinary run's.
- The contrast verdict: the shipped run's pins stay `LOOKS === 'shipped'`
  (Grid horizon's pinned jobs, `LINE_SKIP_CEILING`, the rain owed on Neo, the
  look-pseudo and tide floors); the public looks' `CODES_REQUIRED`, their 1d
  modules, their 1c characters and their 1a clip ratio are skipped; the honest
  step owe (`HONEST_STEPS_OWED`) and the sign's names are owed by the carried
  looks; `the-plan-follows-the-sheets-that-name-data-copied` and its step twin
  read the carried looks' sheets (`FULL_CLASSES`); the page's plan must hold no
  public job off a listed screen.
- Passes: the worn-only road is left to the ordinary run (`geometryPlan` and
  `runnerPasses` with `looks: 'carried'`, held in
  `every-pass-the-runner-runs-is-in-a-coverage-table` and
  `the-runner-runs-every-pass-the-module-lists`). The module-snap check, the
  canaries and the transparency pass run as ever, over the look run's jobs.
- The dump's kind is `carried+<classes>`, compared with its own kind or
  `--within` an ordinary run's.
- Every branch above reads a field of one table (`lookMode`,
  `scripts/probe-modes.mjs`): `carried`, `witnesses`, `publicTogether`,
  `recordsGreen`, `saysGreen`. `the-default-run-turns-no-look-run-branch-on`
  pins the table for every mode by value and holds the runner to it: no
  `CARRIED_RUN`, no `'carried'` literal, every field read. A refactor that
  turned a look-run branch on in the default run would have to change the
  pinned table, or write a condition the test refuses (the critic's P3).

**Its first line** (`scripts/probe-inputs.mjs`, test `probe-inputs.test.mjs`):
the last green `pnpm test:layout` of this checkout and whether the probe's
public inputs moved since. The inputs: every tracked file under `src/`,
`layout/`, `public/`, `workshop/` and `scripts/` (`git ls-files`, hashed from
the working bytes: sources, stylesheets, faces, every piece of art a stylesheet
names, the harness and its fixture look's art, the runner's scripts), less the
tracked fixture's private-look repository, the manuals and the tests; the probe
build's modules outside the tree (the `node_modules` files Rollup loaded,
listed by `probeInputsPlugin` in `vite.probe.config.ts` where
`STALL_PROBE_INPUTS` names, less the private looks' parts); the configs and
the lockfile; Chrome's version, Node's and the tab count. A green ordinary run
records them in `.layout-dump/public-green.json`; the look run hashes them
again before its build and after it. Never a refusal. The first build hashed
the module graph alone, which holds no face and no CSS-only picture: the
critic swapped two faces and the moon and the line said "the same" (P2-1).
Now a planted face and a planted picture are named (`probe-inputs.test.mjs`),
and a fixture, manual or test change is not.

**Red.** The fixture planted with its figure in its ground's colour
(`.item-x { color: var(--s-bg) }`, a planted repository, `plantLooks`): every
geometry pass failed (105 to 577 failures a pass) and the contrast pass with
324 figures below 3:1.

**Runtimes** (this Mac, three tabs; the one-minute load at each start): the
default run 225.0s (2.8) and, after the review's fixes, 231.7s (2.1); the look
run with no selection 41.7s (3.8) and 46.1s (6.5); the default run with the
private look at 0x04 selected 251.1s (3.3); its look run 63.0s (4.6), of which
the geometry walk 8.3s and the contrast pass about 45s, and after the fixes a
back-to-back pair of 66.9s (4.9) and 67.6s (6.9). The stop lines set from
these (D-2026-11-11-05) are PLAN § Open's.

### What the look run does not measure, stated
- **The public looks on every screen but `publish-name`.** They are measured
  by the ordinary run, whose build carries the same private looks as the look
  run's under the same selection — and under a selection, only if somebody runs
  it: the look run's first line says when the last green one was and whether
  the probe's public inputs moved since, and refuses nothing.
- **A carried sheet reaching a public paint by layout.** The DOM test proves
  the public trees do not depend on what the build carries; a carried sheet's
  rule reaching a public element is held at build time by the look lint
  (`lintLookSheet`: every selector under the look's class, never inside
  `:not`, `:is` or `:has`, no sibling combinator after it) and the worn-only
  rules (`wornSheetProblems`), not by a pass. A carried look's faces, masks
  and memory on the page with the public looks (which the plan could not
  separate from contention) are not on the look run's pages at all.
- **The public looks together**: the door's minis, the codes owed by name on
  the public looks' jobs, the shipped run's pinned jobs, the public clip and
  line-skip ceilings, the worn-only road. The ordinary run's.
- **A difference the DOM test does not see**: what a press makes after the
  paint beyond the staging the probe does, a public stall's book naming a
  private decoration's token (`category.ts`; painted on no fixture), and a
  carried look other than the tracked fixture that lists its rows on a public
  screen some other way.
- **The canary reads**, which run through the same per-look clock, are inside
  the per-look contrast figures.

## The wall's own container conditions, for a first-party look (2026-11-11; STEP-WALL-CONTAINER, D-2026-11-11-08)

A first-party look sheet may now hold a top-level `@container sw <condition>`
block for exactly the twelve conditions `LOOK_CONTAINER` lists
(`scripts/workshop-css.mjs`): window.css's own preludes, each entered by a
wall pass on a bare frame. The thirteenth, `(orientation: landscape) and
(max-height: 740px)`, is entered by none and refused with that reason. Inside
a block, layout alone (`CONTAINER_LAYOUT`). The kit still refuses
`@container`; its README is unchanged. No served file changed: window.css,
stall.css, the three look sheets and the app are as on main.

### The table, and which passes enter each condition (bare frame)

Computed by `holds` (`scripts/wall-conditions.mjs`), pinned by value in
`the-wall-conditions-are-window-css-own-and-a-pass-enters-each`, and held to
Chrome on every page by the echo's self-check (below):

| condition | entered by |
|---|---|
| `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 900px)` | desk-wall, short-wall, side-tablet, hd-wall |
| `(orientation: landscape) and (min-height: 901px) and (max-height: 1200px)` | canvas |
| `(orientation: portrait)` | portrait, tablet, tall-tablet, narrow-wall |
| `(orientation: portrait) and (max-height: 1500px)` | tablet, tall-tablet, narrow-wall |
| `(orientation: landscape)` | canvas, desk-wall, short-wall, side-tablet, hd-wall |
| `((orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 900px)) or ((orientation: portrait) and (max-height: 1500px))` | every wall pass but canvas and portrait |
| `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 790px)` | side-tablet, hd-wall |
| `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 870px)` | short-wall, side-tablet, hd-wall |
| `(orientation: portrait) and (max-width: 767.98px)` | narrow-wall |
| `(orientation: landscape) and (max-width: 1919.98px)` | desk-wall, short-wall, side-tablet, hd-wall |
| `(orientation: landscape) and (max-width: 1279.98px)` | side-tablet |
| `(orientation: portrait) and (max-width: 1079.98px)` | tablet, tall-tablet, narrow-wall |
| excluded: `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 740px)` | none (the Awning's 132px puts short-wall, side-tablet and hd-wall under it, by the evaluator and a scratch page in Chrome; the probe's echo does not record 740, being excluded) |

The twelve cut the wall's sizes (short side at least 680) into 21 cells, and
the passes paint 8 (`cellsOf`, held to a dense 4px scan over all thirteen
conditions; PLAN § Open lists the other 13). All thirteen, the excluded 740
among them, cut 24 cells, of which the passes paint 9; the combination rule
reads these (below).

### The static rules (pnpm test)

- `a-look-queries-only-the-walls-own-conditions` and
  `a-container-block-lays-out-and-never-paints` (`look-lint.test.mjs`). Red:
  with the table check removed, the out-of-table plants pass; with the
  allow-list removed, the `color` plant passes.
- `the-wall-conditions-are-window-css-own-and-a-pass-enters-each`
  (`wall-conditions.test.mjs`). Red: desk-wall planted at 1280x901 (the
  matrix differs); a block added to window.css (the table no longer lists
  every prelude, and the matrix and the scan go red with it); the parser made
  to accept an unknown feature (the refusals go red).
- `a-look-uses-no-combination-of-wall-conditions-no-pass-paints`: over every
  first-party sheet a run reads; strict (it refuses). **Since 2026-11-11
  (CRITIC-STEP-8G5's P2) the cells are cut over the look's conditions
  together with window.css's thirteen preludes** (`unpaintedLookCells`,
  `scripts/wall-conditions.mjs`), and every cell where at least one of the
  look's conditions holds must hold a wall pass size; a cell where none
  holds is not asked. Before, the cells were the look's own conditions'
  alone, so a cell the look did not split counted as painted by any pass
  inside it and every single condition passed: the canvas's
  `(orientation: landscape) and (min-height: 901px) and (max-height:
  1200px)` passed on 1920x1080 alone, while at 1280x1024, where
  window.css's `(max-width: 1919.98px)` rules also hold, the private look at
  0x04 covered money in the critic's scratch run (63 failures; 0 with its
  block out). Over all thirteen preludes the wall has 24 cells and the nine
  passes paint 9 of them (the 740 cell and every cell 1920 wide and over
  under 901 tall among the 15 they do not). **No condition is admitted
  alone today**: each of the twelve meets window.css in at least one
  unpainted cell, pinned by value (`VERDICTS`, one example size per cell):
  landscape ≤900 8 cells, landscape 901–1200 2 (990x901 and 1389x901),
  portrait 3, portrait ≤1500 1 (1139x1139), landscape 13, the `or` 9,
  landscape ≤790 4, ≤870 6, portrait ≤767.98 wide 1 (680x1709), landscape
  ≤1919.98 wide 8, ≤1279.98 wide 5, portrait ≤1079.98 wide 2. So the lint
  admits the block and this rule refuses it: no first-party look may hold
  an `@container sw` block until more wall passes exist, and the tracked
  fixture's inert block (`order: 0` under landscape ≤900) was taken out —
  the guard has no passing public subject. Plants: the canvas's condition
  alone refused, its sentence naming 990x901 and 1389x901 with the
  window.css conditions that meet it there (1280x1024 stands in the
  1389x901 cell), and refused still with a 1280x1024 size added (990x901
  left); {landscape ≤900, portrait ≤1500}, accepted before, refused (9
  cells). The accepting branch, over sizes added in the test: the canvas's
  condition with 1280x1024 and 1200x960, portrait ≤1500 with 1080x1080,
  portrait ≤767.98 wide with 720x1600. Red: the rule put back to the old
  cells (`unpaintedCells` over the look's conditions alone), the two plant
  refusals fail (2 of 13, `combo-cells-tools/red-old-rule.log`).
- `a-container-rule-is-not-out-ranked-by-a-later-base-rule` (theme-sheets):
  red on both shapes in a planted private look; the covering check off, red;
  selectors split at every comma, red (and a false take-back on a real sheet).
- `ladderRules` unwraps `@container`: reverted, the planted container-block
  money size passes `a-look-never-sizes-inside-a-money-node`.
- `audit-shadowing.mjs` descends `@container` as conditional; reverted, the
  planted window.css consumer stays SHADOWED. Its output on main is identical
  before and after (window.css's container blocks read no `--s-` var).
- `every-sheet-reader-descends-a-container-block` (`sheet-readers.test.mjs`):
  23 readers of `@media` in `scripts/`, `layout/` and the src tests, 7 listed
  as descending `@container`, 16 not relevant with the reason; red on an
  unlisted reader, a stale entry, an entry with no reason, and a descending
  reader that never names `container` (in-test plants).

### The probe rules (pnpm test:layout)

- **`the-wall-condition-echo-agrees-with-this-chrome`**: the page adopts one
  constructed sheet that sets `--probe-wall-cq-<i>` on the wall frame's
  children under each `LOOK_CONTAINER` condition, on for the whole page; once
  a page, hidden frames (`container: sw / size`) at every wall pass size, at
  1280x900 under 132px of top padding, and at a square, 1280x901, 767.98 and
  1279.98 wide, each have their echo held to `holds`. Clean tree: 12
  conditions over 14 frames on 15 pages, every one agreed. Red (`holds` with
  every max bound one pixel tight, through `pnpm test:layout:look`): three
  disagreements on every one of the 15 pages (1280x900, 767.98 wide, 1279.98
  wide). A page with no record fails the run.
- **`every-wall-cell-a-look-uses-is-painted`**: every wall paint records the
  echo off the painted frame, by look and variant; the runner reads each
  measured look's own sheet and fails a look and variant whose combinations
  were not all entered on some wall paint of the run. Printed on every run
  ("wall conditions entered, by look and pass"). Clean tree when it landed:
  the tracked fixture used one condition, both combinations painted on every
  variant (since 2026-11-11 the fixture carries no block, the static rule
  refusing every condition alone, and a default run prints "no measured look
  uses one": this rule owes nothing on a public run; it still owes a look's
  own cells, not the cells crossed with window.css's, which the static rule
  now holds);
  Modern under the Awning enters 790 and 870 at 1280x900 and 790 at 1280x800,
  as the evaluator says for a content box 132px shorter. Red (a planted look
  using the 901–1200 condition and padding its own frame 200px, which the
  static rule cannot see): every variant fails, the canvas's content box
  1920x880 entering ≤900 instead.
- **`the-wall-code-never-paints-below-its-floor`**: every code under the
  frame paints at least `WINDOW_QR_MIN_PX` (280) on its side, its turn
  undone, half a pixel allowed; every wall pass owes a read on every look. A
  code with no box is not read here: 1a fails it ("has no box at all"; the
  build critic's plant B, a code at 0x0 at the tablet, 84 failures, all 1a's).
  Clean tree: 0 failures. Red (planted looks through the look run): the code
  at 200px fails every wall pass (69–84 a pass) and the desktop page pass
  (15); the same rule inside the ≤900 landscape block fails only desktop,
  desk-wall, short-wall, side-tablet and hd-wall.

### After the build critic (D-2026-11-11-09)

The critic proved the promise "a container block only lays out, so nothing
paints differently per composition" false three ways; each is closed or
stated.

- **`a-look-never-reads-the-rung-count`** (P1-1, look lint): a wall
  composition may set `--name-rungs`, and a rule at rest that read it
  (`opacity: calc((var(--name-rungs, 6) - 1) / 5)`, plant A) painted the
  status line at opacity 0 on the portrait walls and 1 on the canvas, every
  pass green. A first-party sheet reads `--name-rungs` nowhere (only the
  ladder script does). Red: with the rule off, plant A and four other reads
  (in a media block, a keyframe, a custom property) pass. Cost nil: no sheet
  read it.
- **The plate's notes are held lines** (P1-2, probe): `.sw-pay-note`
  (`PAY_NOTE_DIRECT`, `PAY_NOTE_FINAL`, the feeds' disagreement) joins
  `WALL_HELD`, and a held line is now read by its own box as well: laid out
  at no height or width, or hiding its own text by its own overflow, while
  rendered and holding text, it fails `nothing-on-the-wall-is-cut-from-below`
  (the control check skipped a box with no area before, so the critic's
  `max-height: 0` read as absent). Red through the look run on a planted
  look (`overflow: hidden` at rest, `max-height: 0` under the portrait ≤1500
  condition): 30 failures each at tablet, tall-tablet and narrow-wall, and
  none elsewhere; with `max-height: 6px` instead, 90 ("hides 33px of its
  own text from below"). Clean tree green, the controls read rising by 30 a
  wall pass.
- **`a-look-never-divides-by-a-length`** (P1-3, look lint): inside a math
  function a first-party sheet divides only by a number; a divisor holding
  a length or percentage, a `var()`, an `env()` or an `attr()` is refused
  (`lengthDivisors`). The critic's plants (an opacity by `cqh`, an opacity by
  `vh` on a money node, a colour by `cqw`) and five more are refused; red with
  the rule off. Green on the shipped looks, stall.css, window.css, broadcast.css,
  the fixtures, the canary and the private look at 0x04 (its 47 divisions are
  by numbers). **Known gap, stated**: a steep `clamp()` of `cq` or viewport
  units (`clamp(0px, (100cqh - 1050px) * 1000, 9999px)`) still makes a
  layout step at any size; not closed (PLAN § Open).

## A mood's variants, and the look run's line (2026-11-11; D-2026-11-11-17, D-2026-11-11-18)

The private look at 0x04 gained two moods (8h). Each mood is an all-worn
variant of every contrast job the look owes (`wornAllFlags`, one per mood),
so the look's contrast jobs went from 116 to 316, and three things the probe
read for one variant had to read for each.

**The line-skip ceiling is per variant.** `CARRIED_LINE_SKIP_CEILING`
(`scripts/look-tallies.mjs`) was one sum per viewport and kind, measured on
the bare variant alone; with two moods the counts tripled, and a sum let a
mood's skips absorb a bare-look regression or a mood's own clip ride under
the bare count. It is keyed by variant now, as the probe names them
(`skipVariantOf`: `bare`, `worn` for `0xffff`, `flags <n>` for each further
mood's all-worn state, the names the 1d tallies already print), and a
variant measured that its entry does not name fails the run, and so does a
variant it names that the run measured no job of (a mood's jobs gone from
the plan read as no skips; the critic's P3-1). The runner
prints each carried look's sum, each variant beside it, and each variant's
skips by screen. Test: `holds each variant to its own ceiling, so a mood’s
skips cannot hide a bare look’s` (the trade of one line bare for one under
the mood, sums equal, fails; a new mood's variant with no entry fails; a
named variant with no job measured fails). The
tracked fixture's entry was split from the default run's dump: bare and
worn alike, mobile 8/5 and desktop 2/4, canvas 105/0 bare and 102/0 worn
(the ticker's 3 are painted bare only). The private look at 0x04's, measured
by the look run with its two moods: mobile 8/5 and desktop 3/4 under every
variant, canvas 104/0 bare and 101/0 under each mood (sums 24/15, 9/12,
306/0, the 8h builder's). Its bare desktop count fell from 7 to 3: the five
`studio-items` lines of 2026-10-12, marked provisional then, are two today.

**A private mood moves the look's red.** `PaletteDelta` names `danger`, read
from a private look's mood alone (`MOOD_ONLY_PALETTE_KEYS`, `lookData.ts`).
`--s-danger` is `legibleOn` the surface **and the removal warning's own tint
of it** (`dangerInk`, `theme.ts`: `.warn` is danger text on 6% danger over
the surface, and no fixture shows removal mode, so no pass reads it; the
critic's P2-1, whose red rgb(176,73,58) on rgb(28,32,34) reads 3.02:1 on the
surface and 2.89:1 on the tint, and is corrected now). Every shipped look
and mood clears both, so no shipped colour moves
(`a-looks-red-reads-on-the-warnings-tint`); the public entry script grows
by the check. **What reads a danger line on any other ground is the contrast

Seen on the look run with a stand-in mood red on `publish-name`'s `p.ctx`,

**A private mood's art under text is listed, in its own sheet alone.**
`PRIVATE_DECORATION_ART` (`decor-gate.test.ts`), keyed by the look's class,

`.stall.<look>.att-<mood>`, or an open `.sheet` under it, and
`background-image` alone (the critic's P3-2: a descendant or a
`background-color` key would let a later entry lay a slab under a figure).
The private look at 0x04's mood class `att-rubbing` has two: a mood's own

**The look run's line is 240s, and the selected full run is no longer a

## Step 8i, A: nodes below the goods, and a private row's reasons (2026-11-15; D-2026-11-15-05)

The public half of step 8i's first step (STEP-8I-PLAN v2.4, A). Two probe
rules and the decor gate's read of a private look's `guard.json`; the static
half is in `src/ui/decor-gate.test.ts` and `layout/movingDecor.test.ts`, and
CLAUDE.md §4 and §6 say where each lives. The plan named the two probe rules
and the render test after one look's own rows; in tracked files they are
named for the mechanism (the words rule): the still-box rule is
`a-file-below-the-goods-is-painted-once-on-a-still-box`, and the render test
`the-nodes-below-the-goods-mount-only-what-is-worn`.

### `a-node-below-the-goods-shows-in-the-first-fold-of-a-short-stall`

The billboard's first-fold rule is a product rule (the beetle was found below
the fold, which is why the yard moved under the sign), and a node a look
stands after the goods (`below-goods`, step 8f1) is below the fold of a long
shop by construction. The owner's rule for it (Q4): **worn alone, its box
stands wholly inside the scroll region's showing part** (the region's box
inside the viewport, above the dock) **at rest on the two short screens**,
`sparse` and `empty`, **and once `offers` is scrolled to its end**; some part
of it inside the showing part across, so a node pushed sideways off the page
is not read as shown. `above-dock` keeps the billboard's own first fold on
`offers`. Read on every page the billboard paints (every pass but the short
ones), per look (`belowGoodsByClass`, short/end); the tracked fixture, whose
two node rows stand below the goods, owes reads of both on both page passes
(`probe-coverage.mjs`).

### `a-file-below-the-goods-is-painted-once-on-a-still-box`

(Narrowed by the still-painter step, below: the second half now binds a box
that paints art more than one row names, and a row's own art may move.)

Rows that stand below the goods may share a piece of art, painted once on the
first of them worn (the 8i plan's spike (a): a mask on the node clips its own
pseudo-elements, so the shared piece goes on the first node's `::after`). On
every paint, among the below-the-goods nodes the paint wears and their
`::before` and `::after`: **a file is named by one box at most** (any
property that draws one: a background or border image, a mask or mask
border, a list marker, a pseudo's `content`; every `url()` the computed value
names), and **a box that names a file runs no animation, nor does the node it
hangs on** (an animation on the node carries its pseudo-elements; read from
the computed `animation-name` and the document's running animations). A box
with no box (`display: none`, a pseudo with no `content`) names nothing.
Per look (`stillPainterByClass`, the boxes naming a file read); the tracked
fixture owes reads on both page passes.

### The fixture's subjects

Two unminted node rows below the goods (bits 3 and 4, slots of the look's
own), and a `guard.json` for all four rows. The first worn carries one still
tile on its `::after` (`:is(<both>):not(:is(<both>) ~ *)::after`, the
fixture's `ground.svg`); the first paints its own `::before` and the second
its own box, in the tokens. **The second turns its own node** by a degree
about its foot, **and only where it stands after the first**, which then
carries the tile: worn alone it carries the tile and stands still. The turn
is on the node and not on its `::before` because 1b reads a look's
pseudo-element moved by a transform as standing anywhere and fails it where
it paints (`pseudoRegion`; measured below). Nothing of either paints on the
wall (`display: none` under `.shop-window`). The default run's contrast plan
does not move (796 jobs with the fixture, 634 public: the fixture's jobs are
the skeleton's cells, bare and all worn, and its new rows are worn in the
all-worn variant); its boxes do.

## Step 8i, B: a mood's page art at its worst (2026-11-16; D-2026-11-15-06)

`a-mood-art-layer-is-read-at-its-worst`. Page art stands still while the
content scrolls over it, so a line on the bare ground passes over every
patch of it, as a drop of Neo's rain crosses every line in time; the
contrast pass read it at one scroll position (PLAN § Open's at-rest entry,
the mood-hooks critic's P3-3). This closes it for every job that wears a
mood (D-2026-11-14-01's open item). The model is `layout/moodArt.ts`, pure
and unit-tested (`moodArt.test.ts`); the page's half is `moodArtAtItsWorst`
in `probe.ts`; the runner holds it in `contrastPrepare` and `moodEcho`. The
fix round after its critic (`CRITIC-MOOD-FLATTEN.md`, D-2026-11-16-03) is
folded in below and its proofs are under "The fix round".

**What it flattens.** In every pass-4 contrast job that wears a mood
(`wearsMood`), every `background-image` layer on the stall's root, on an
open `.sheet` under it and on the scroll region (`.stall-scroll`): the
mood's own art, the layers it shares with the bare look, and the page art
of the decorations worn with it. A bare job is left alone and reports so;
the transparency pass does not ask. Each element's background is read
whole and rewritten, important (so no animation moves it), as flat
rectangles of the worst ground its search finds the stack of layers can
put under a line there (`worstCells`); its background colour stays. The
root's, an open sheet's and the region's stacks are searched apart, each
over its own background colour.

- **A gradient** (`linear`, `radial`, `conic`, repeating or not) by every
  colour on every segment between two consecutive stops, `SEGMENT_SAMPLES`
  (32) steps each in premultiplied sRGB: its strongest stop is among them,
  and so is a point between two stops of different hue, which can be darker
  than either (a composite's luminance along a segment is convex, so its
  maximum is a stop and its minimum may lie between). A transition hint
  moves where the colours fall, not which, and is passed over.
- **A file** rasterised in the page at its painted size (a canvas, the
  file's URL; read once a page for each URL and size) and read back, every
  distinct pixel.
- **The stack, not one layer at a time** (`worstStack`): one layer at a
  time, an opaque scrap on top would hide a darker one on the layer below
  that shows wherever the top is transparent — Rural's confetti is three
  such tiles. A stack of at most `EXHAUSTIVE_LIMIT` (200,000) combinations of
  one colour a layer is searched whole (`exhaustiveStack`); past it, by a
  **beam** (`beamStack`): the `BEAM` (12) composites the judge reads lowest
  at each layer and, beside them, the composites at each extreme of every
  premultiplied channel and of alpha. Both pinned by value. A beam is a
  search, not a proof: on 1,000 seeded small stacks it misses the whole
  search on some, and reads no lower than it on any. The runner prints, per
  look and variant, how many stacks each read searched whole and by the
  beam (on the shipped run, Rural's Sun-faded all-worn stacks are searched by
  the beam: its confetti and grain rasters put them past the limit). A
  search is reused across jobs by the layers' ids and what the judge reads.
  Since the still-painter step every stack that goes to the beam is searched
  again, once a page, with a beam of 256, and the lower read is painted
  (below, "The still painter").

**(a) Toward which ink.** The worst ground is chosen for the mood's own
`--s-text` (`judgeFor`): of every colour the stack can paint at a point,
composited over the element's background colour on the mood's `--s-bg`, the
one that reads least against it — the darkest on a light mood, the lightest
on a dark one. That is the worst for every ink on the text's side of the
ground while the art stays on the ground's side of that ink. Where the art
can reach past an ink toward the text, the painted ground is past it too,
and that ink's own worst (a ground near its own luminance) is not painted.
**The condition** (the critic's P3-6): if that ink still clears 3:1 on the
painted ground, the text there reads at most a third of its own contrast
with that ink — under 3:1 for any ink within 9:1 of the text — so a line
in the text's ink on that same cell fails, and the job with it; if the ink
does not clear 3:1 on it, it fails itself. **Not read at its worst,
stated:** an ink that clears 3:1 on the painted ground on a cell where no
line in the text's ink stands; an ink further than 9:1 from the text; a line
whose ink is on the other side of the ground (a light line on a light
mood's ground). No shipped mood's ink or the fixture's is in that gap today
(the critic's survey).

**(b) What area.** A layer that repeats along an axis covers its clip area
along it. Along an axis it does not repeat, its tile stands still while the
content of a scroller scrolls over it. The capture stands every scroller at
its start — checked, not assumed: a scroller not at its start when the
flatten reads, or when its writes are read back after the freeze, refuses
the job — so a line reaches the tile only from below (or the right), and
only as far as the scroller's range carries it: for every scroller
(`overflow` `auto`, `scroll` or `overlay`) along that axis whose box the tile
reaches, the tile is widened to the band from its part inside the scroller
to that part's end plus the range, cut to the scroller's box, across the
span the tile covers on the other axis — not the whole page, and not only
the tile. In the band, and in the tile of a layer so widened, the layer may
also be absent (the line has scrolled off it), so a transparent colour is
among its own. The range is the scroller's own overflow, or, for the boxes
the capture grows to show everything (the region, an open sheet), at most
how far the capture grew the page past the job's own height, which the
runner hands over: an upper bound, read at the contrast pass's heights
(844, 900 and 1080) and no other — a shorter screen sweeps a wider band. A
scroller that cannot move widens nothing, and a tile that meets no scroller
is read where it is. `local` attachment moves with the element's own
content, so it is read where it is only on a box that scrolls itself, and
widened there for the scrollers inside it. A layer the element animates the
position or size of covers its whole clip area, and may be absent.

*Why the range* (the build's own first run): widened over the scroller's
whole box, Modern's empty stall under After hours read 2.20:1 at both
widths — the awning's accent spill under the empty shelf's second line, a
line on a screen too short to scroll at all. A line no scroll carries
there is no reader of it.

**(c) Size, position and clip.** Each layer's own computed size, position
(`background-position-x`/`-y`, `calc()` of a percentage and a length read),
repeat, origin box and clip box, cycled over the layers as CSS cycles them,
give its tiles in the element's border box. Every cut is rounded to a whole
pixel, so two rectangles meet and never overlap (an overlap of two
translucent rectangles would composite twice, a false red), and each is
written in px from the border box, `no-repeat`, border-box origin and
clip. **Read back** (the critic's P2-1): after the freeze, just before the
capture, every flattened element's seven background longhands are read
against a hidden reference element given the same declarations
(`moodWritesHeld`, `__moodArtHeld`), so a transition on a background
longhand, a value the browser dropped, or a write that never landed refuses
the job with a sentence, where the report would have said flattened.

**(d) What cannot be read** is a sentence the runner refuses the job on,
never a skip: an image that is neither a file nor a gradient this models
(`image-set()`, a prefixed gradient, `cross-fade()`); a gradient
interpolated in a space written other than sRGB, or with a stop outside
sRGB (`oklch()`, `lab()`, `color(display-p3 …)`); a gradient with a
`color(srgb …)` stop and no space written — every `color-mix()` computes to
one, and Chrome then interpolates in OKLab (blue to yellow paints (108, 172,
198) at its midpoint where sRGB paints (128, 128, 127), the critic's) —
wherever two consecutive stops are distinct, both visible and at two
positions (a segment to or from transparent, a hard stop, or one colour
held paints the same in either space and is read); a size, position or
repeat it does not parse; a file layer at `auto`, `cover` or `contain` (its
intrinsic size is not read); a `fixed` attachment, and `local` on a box
that does not scroll itself (it stands still while a scroller inside it
moves); a `text` clip; on a box the capture grew, a tile placed along y, or
sized along y where it does not repeat down (a file's, at any repeat), by a
non-zero percentage (the grown capture would put it elsewhere than the
job's own height); a still tile under scrollers on two axes (the corner
reached by scrolling both is not modelled). And, on the page: a file that
does not load or cannot be read back; a background colour it cannot read; a
`transform`, `rotate`, `scale`, `translate` or `zoom` on the element or
above it; a blend mode other than `normal`; a scroller not at its start;
and a stall whose `--s-text` or `--s-bg` does not resolve to an opaque
colour.

**Owed.** Every full prepare of a pass-4 job reports what it flattened
(`moodArt`: whether it wears a mood, the elements read by kind, the open
sheets and scroll regions on the paint counted apart from the read — with
the same `.sheet` and `.stall-scroll` class queries, scoped to the whole app
rather than to each stall, so not a second road: a sheet or region outside
every stall is caught, a renamed class is the fixture owes' to catch — the layers
and rectangles by the kind of element, the stacks searched each way, the
read-back; zero layers is a report, and a paint that wears no mood says
so). The runner refuses a job whose prepare reports nothing, read no stall
root, read fewer sheets or regions than the page counts, was not read back,
or flattened without a mood; and the page publishes the jobs that wear a
mood (`__contrastOwed().mood`, `moodOwed`, derived at run time from its plan
and the looks' own rows, never a tracked table), and the walk is held to it
at its end, both ways. **The tracked fixture's mood jobs owe the art**: on
every one, file layers and painted rectangles, and a layer read on every
open sheet and every scroll region the paint holds; over them, at least one
sheet and one region read with a layer — so a flatten that read nothing
fails on the public run. **And the flatten is held to its effect on every
contrast page** (`the-mood-flatten-paints-a-planted-ground`, the shape of
`the-ground-read-fails-a-planted-ground`): before the page's first job, the
real `flattenMoodArt` runs on a box planted over everything at the top left
— a white ground, an opaque black still tile across its top, a scroller
whose content moves 400px under it — and the runner captures the page and
reads the planted line's box, 120px below the tile: every pixel must read
black within two levels, where at rest it reads white; the plant's own
write is read back like a job's; a page with no record fails. **What it
covers, stated** (the re-check's P3-3): one kind of layer on one kind of
element, a gradient on a root-like box banded along y. A file rasterised
and read back, the sheet's and the region's roads, a band along x, the
stack search and that the cells line up with the paint rest on the
fixture's owes above and on the plants made once (below). The dump's
job record carries what was flattened (never the time). A failing line in
such a job says the job read its mood's page art at its worst, and the
runner prints, per look and variant, the jobs, the layers by kind and by
element, the rectangles, the stacks searched each way, the least read, the
least line read and the flatten's own tab time. The plan's mood keys on the
shipped run are pinned by count (162: Modern's 80 all-worn jobs and Rural's
82, its two stilled `unbuyable` jobs among them), 242 with the tracked
fixture.

## The still painter: a row's own art below the goods may move, and a keyframe key keeps its prefix (2026-11-17; D-2026-11-17-02)

A public step before the private slice that moves rows below the goods. The
8i-2 critic's P1-1: `a-file-below-the-goods-is-painted-once-on-a-still-box`
(step 8i, A, above) failed every box below the goods that named a file and
ran an animation, or hung on a node that ran one. The movers that slice
plans move a row's own art, so the rule failed them, though what it protects
(D-2026-11-15-05, Q2) is art more than
one row paints: a ground every row stands on, carried by the first worn, that
a moving carrier would move under the rows beside it. This step narrows the
rule to that, fixes how the probe names a vendor-prefixed keyframe key (the
same critic's P3-2), and carries the mood-flatten re-check's three P3s.

### `a-file-below-the-goods-is-painted-once-on-a-still-box`, narrowed

On every paint, as before: **a file is named by one box at most** among the
below-the-goods nodes the paint wears and their `::before` and `::after`.
The second half is now judged **at the end of each page run, per look**
(`judgeStillPainters`, `layout/stillPainter.ts`, pure and unit-tested in
`stillPainter.test.ts`; the probe's half gathers on every paint and judges
after its main loop):

- **Shared art** is a file that boxes on the nodes of **more than one row**
  named on that run. Which rows paint a file is what the probe saw: it paints
  each row alone on every screen that is not a state screen (`wornVariants`),
  and every row worn together, so the shared tile the first worn carries is
  named by each row's node when that row is alone.
- **A box that paints shared art runs no animation, nor does the node it
  hangs on.** A box that moves and names only its own row's art passes and is
  counted; its motion is read by 1a, 1b, 1c and the keyframe reads, as any
  motion is.
- **Fail closed**: a moving box naming a file, on a run where some other
  below-the-goods row of the look was never painted alone with a node
  mounted, cannot be told own art (that row alone might carry the same file),
  and fails, naming the rows never painted alone.
- **Counted per look**, on every pass's coverage line
  (`stillPainterByClass`): the boxes naming a file read, the files shared,
  the box reads painting them, and the moving box reads that paint their
  row's own art. The tracked fixture owes all four on both page passes
  (`probe-coverage.mjs`; its gaps are pinned in `probe-coverage.test.mjs`).

**Why this definition.** The rule's target is what the paints show, and the
probe already paints each row alone, so the set of rows that paint a file is
read off Chrome's own computed styles; it needs no reading of selectors (a
shared piece is laid by an `:is()` of every row with a `:not(… ~ *)`, which a
static reader would have to match). A stricter shape was weighed and not
taken: holding every file a moving box names to the look's guard keys. It
reads a sheet, not a paint, and a guard key names a box, not which rows
reach it.

**The fixture's subject.** The turning row (it turns its own node by a degree,
and only where it stands after the first row) carries a mark of its own,
`turn.svg`, on its `::before`, which no other row names: so a row's own art
on a moving box has a public subject, beside the shared tile on a still box.
Its guard names the key (`.att-fixture-turn::before | background-image`) and
its `underMood` and `moving` reasons say the mark is there. Re-pinned: the
fixture's art list in `served-sheets.test.mjs` and `look-lint.test.mjs`. The
default run's contrast plan does not move.

Read on the fixture's look run at the tip (both page passes): 203 boxes
naming a file, 1 shared file (the tile), 107 box reads painting it, and 85
moving box reads painting their row's own art (the mark on the turning
node, in every all-worn paint); 0 on every wall pass, where the fixture hides
both rows. Which reads see that motion, stated: 1b leaves the turning node
out as a move of a box that holds nothing 1b reads (the mark is an in-flow
pseudo-element with no paint that reaches), with the same seek counts as on
`main` (1,315 at 390, 1,702 at 1280 on the default run, both); the geometry
passes' decoration sweep holds its box off every protected box over time,
as before.

### A keyframe key keeps its prefix (`keyframeKeys.ts`)

Chrome's `getKeyframes()` names a longhand it holds only under a vendor
prefix with the prefix in lower case and no dash. Measured in Chrome 157
(`keyframes` set from `initial` to `inherit` for every property its computed
style lists, 491 in all): 34 keys come back prefixed, and an unprefixed
`mask-position` comes back as `webkitMaskPositionX` and
`webkitMaskPositionY`, its longhands in Chrome. The probe's mapping put a
dash before each capital and none before the prefix, so it read
`webkit-mask-position-x`, a name no list holds. One mapping now,
`keyframeProperty` (a custom property as it is, `cssFloat` and `cssOffset` as
`float` and `offset`, a `webkit`, `Webkit`, `moz`, `Moz`, `ms` or `Ms` prefix
before a capital as `-webkit-`, `-moz-`, `-ms-`), and `keyframeValue` for a
value by its longhand; every keyframe read goes through it (1b's seek and its
keyframe-values road, 1a's end read, the keyframe-offset reads,
`movesOtherBoxes`, `groundOnly`, `outerShadowOnly`, the dress rule's
`animationFaults`, and 1c's trigger, whose own mapping already gave a
`webkit` key its dash). Unit-tested over the 34 keys
(`keyframe-keys-are-the-longhands-chrome-names`).

**What the fixed names now match, list by list**, and whether that reads
less:

- `REACH_NEEDLESS` (1b leaves an animation of only these alone): now matches
  `-webkit-mask-position-x`/`-y` and the five `-webkit-mask-box-image-*`
  longhands. **Less work, nothing unread**: 1b reads every paint unclipped by
  its own clip-path or mask (the list's own reason), and a mask moves no box
  and adds no paint; the unprefixed mask longhands were on it already.
- `MOVES_NO_OTHER_BOX` (1b's "wide" read; the keyframe-offset read's seek for
  every figure's self-clip read, `movesOtherBoxes`): now matches the two mask
  position longhands, the five mask box image longhands,
  `-webkit-text-fill-color`, `-webkit-text-stroke-color` and
  `-webkit-text-stroke-width`. **Less work, nothing unread**: none of them
  lays out a box (a text stroke paints over its glyphs; a mask clips paint),
  so no box but the animated one can move, and that one is still read where
  it paints. 1b reads no text stroke at all, so a stroke read "wide" or
  "still" reads the same; the first-party lint refuses a text stroke and fill
  outright.
- `DRESS_HELD` through `animationFaults` (a money node's own keyframes, by
  their values, at rest): now holds `-webkit-text-fill-color`,
  `-webkit-text-stroke-width`, `-webkit-text-security`,
  `-webkit-text-decorations-in-effect`, `-webkit-line-clamp`,
  `-webkit-box-reflect` and `-webkit-mask-box-image-source`. **Stricter**: a
  keyframe setting one of them on a money node was not held by its values
  before (the offset read, which reads computed styles, held them at the
  offsets).
- `BOX_HELD` through `keyframeHeld` (a box above a figure, by its keyframes'
  values): now holds `-webkit-box-reflect` and
  `-webkit-mask-box-image-source`. **Stricter.**
- No other list a keyframe name is looked up in (`SEEK_NEEDLESS`,
  `SEEK_ON_OWN`, `GROUND_ONLY`, `END_MOOT_PROPS`, `ANCHOR_FOLLOWED`,
  `REACH_FROM_VALUES`, `REACH_INHERITED`, `KEYFRAME_SIZES`,
  `OFFSET_GEOMETRY`, 1c's `PAINT_ONLY_ANIMATION`) holds a longhand Chrome
  names with a prefix: `-webkit-filter` and `-webkit-box-shadow` are aliases
  Chrome names unprefixed. Unchanged.

On the fixture, a `mask-position` animation on the turning row's own mark
(plant G1, below): 1b seeks it **0** times wide at 390, 1280 and 360, and
leaves 96 more animations alone as needless (158, from 62); the same plant
under the old mapping (G1-old) is seeked **192** times wide at 390 and 1280
and 110 at 360 (1b's seeks 0.18s a pass against 0.02s), and the
keyframe-offset read seeks it for every figure's self-clip read on 95
animations (1,218 self-clip reads a pass, against 32).

### The mood flatten's re-check (`CRITIC-MOOD-FLATTEN-2.md`, P3-1 to P3-3)

- **P3-1, the beam on the stacks that use it.** Every stack that goes to the
  beam is searched again, once a page (the page's cache keeps the result),
  with a beam of 256 (`WIDE_BEAM`, pinned by value beside `BEAM` and
  `EXHAUSTIVE_LIMIT`): **the lower of the two reads is the one painted**,
  and each miss is counted (`SearchTally.wide`) and printed with both reads
  under the flatten's own lines. **Printed, not failed**: a miss says the
  narrow search was short, not that a line fails, and a failure there would
  red a look whose every line clears the worse ground, with nothing its
  author could change; printing alone would leave the job read on a ground
  that is not the worst the probe found. Painting the lower closes both. The
  wide beam is a search too. Measured: no stack read lower on the default
  run (Rural's Sun-faded beam stacks: 13, 0 lower), on the fixture's look
  run (Rural's two on `publish-name`, 0 lower) or under the private look at
  0x04's selection (its second mood's eight to nine a run, 0 lower). Its cost
  there, the flatten's own tab time: the private look's second mood 2.1–2.3s
  against 1.3–1.6s on 8i-2's runs, Rural's two stacks 0.3s against 0.03s;
  on the default run, Rural's thirteen 2.79s against 0.49s on `main` (about
  0.8s of wall time at three tabs). The model's own case:
  a seeded stack the beam of 12 misses, sent past the limit by a top layer of
  transparent colours, reads lower under the wide beam, and the lower is
  returned and the miss counted (`moodArt.test.ts`); the unit tests' own
  synthetic 450-colour stack is missed by the narrow beam too (1.000381:1
  against 1.000333:1).
- **P3-2, "another road".** The sheet and region counts are taken with the
  same `.sheet` and `.stall-scroll` class queries as the read, scoped to
  `#app` rather than to each stall: a sheet or region outside every stall is
  caught, a renamed class is not; the fixture's owes are what catch that. The
  comments in `probe.ts`, `layout-check.mjs` and this file's Step 8i, B entry
  say so now.
- **P3-3, the planted check's scope.** It covers one kind of layer on one
  kind of element: a gradient on a root-like box, banded along y. A file's
  raster, the sheet's and the region's roads, a band along x, the stack search
  and that the cells line up with the paint rest on the fixture's owes and on
  the plants made once. Said in its docblock and in Step 8i, B.
